USMLE-style practice · Pathology

A damaged arterial wall

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with an immune-mediated vasculitis undergoes biopsy. A small artery has intensely eosinophilic material within its wall, loss of normal mural cells, and deposited plasma proteins. Which pattern of tissue injury is most likely?

  1. Fat necrosis
  2. Caseous necrosis
  3. Liquefactive necrosis
  4. Coagulative necrosis of parenchyma
  5. Fibrinoid necrosis
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Fibrinoid necrosis

Severe vascular injury can produce fibrin-like eosinophilic deposits in vessel walls, termed fibrinoid necrosis.

Understanding the options

Fibrinoid necrosis
Severe vascular injury can produce fibrin-like eosinophilic deposits in vessel walls, termed fibrinoid necrosis.
Fat necrosis
Fat necrosis involves adipocytes and often calcium soaps.
Caseous necrosis
Caseation produces granular debris in a granulomatous lesion.
Liquefactive necrosis
Liquefaction describes digestion of tissue into liquid.
Coagulative necrosis of parenchyma
Parenchymal coagulation does not identify the characteristic vessel-wall pattern.
